reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining AirBit Club by placing Bitcoin into a trading pool, promises stated profits after seven days and profit sharing for up to 525 business days, and links recruitment growth to commissions. It also presents residual retirement income across as many as 63 levels and directly instructs viewers to start the business with once-in-a-lifetime framing.

citations.quote: After you join the club with any of the memberships available, we will use those bitcoins to place them in a pool to start trading cryptocurrencies.
And after 7 days that you join, you will start gaining Bitcoin profits from the AirBit pool.
AirBit Club will share up to 50% of profits and will split among all club members.
this is called mining.
we will use those bitcoins to place them in a pool to start trading cryptocurrencies.

opening.argument: The presentation distinguishes Bitcoin’s potential from certainty: it says the technology has “the potential” to grow, and describes the club as sharing “up to” 50% of profits. Its discussion of affiliate participation also acknowledges uncertainty, noting that repeat purchases are “not guarantee[d].” Those qualifications matter: the video does not say every participant will earn a fixed amount or that Bitcoin’s value must rise. A judge should assess it as optimistic, conditional commentary about a volatile technology and a proposed program, not treat every favorable projection as proof of deceptive intent.

citations.quote: technology that has the potential to be bigger than the internet
AirBit Club will share up to 50% of profits
but not guarantee to buy products the second time

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s quoted pool and seven-day statements describe how the program says it operates; they do not establish that a particular return is guaranteed. Its reference to “up to 50%” itself preserves variability. And recruitment commissions do not, without more, prove that the Bitcoin trading offer is fictitious. The opening’s aspirational language and qualifications make certainty an unwarranted inference.

citations.quote: After you join the club with any of the memberships available, we will use those bitcoins to place them in a pool to start trading cryptocurrencies.
AirBit Club will share up to 50% of profits and will split among all club members.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Up to” limits the stated share of profits; it does not qualify the promise that members will start gaining Bitcoin profits after seven days or that distributions continue for up to 525 business days. The cited non-guarantee concerns whether affiliates’ teams will buy products again, not whether AirBit’s pool will generate member profits. Potential growth language about Bitcoin likewise does not caution viewers about the club’s returns.

citations.quote: And after 7 days that you join, you will start gaining Bitcoin profits from the AirBit pool.
For every membership, AirBit Club will share profits for up to 525 business days.
not guarantee to buy products the second time

opening.argument: The video devotes substantial attention to explaining Bitcoin: what decentralization means, how mining works, why supply is limited, and how its price changed over time. It introduces itself as help to “understand and discover” Bitcoin, and explains trading with a numerical buy-and-sell example. The AirBit Club discussion is presented within that technology and operations lesson, rather than as a bare request for money. That framing supports treating the central material as an educational explanation of cryptocurrency and a particular platform’s claimed mechanics, not assuming that its promotional tone alone establishes a scam.

citations.quote: this video is to help you understand and discover one of the biggest inventions after the internet, Bitcoin!
this is called mining.
Trading is to buy and sell cryptocurrencies.
For example, eRbit buys 1,000 Bitcoins at $612 and sells those Bitcoins at $615.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The Bitcoin background and trading example are relevant context, not proof that this is merely a tutorial. The opening does not address the later explanation of membership, pooled funds, recurring profits, or commissions. But explaining a service’s proposed operating model is still different from independently verifying its claims; the prosecution’s excerpts establish what the video says, not whether the pool actually trades or whether distributions occur as described.

citations.quote: After you join the club with any of the memberships available, we will use those bitcoins to place them in a pool to start trading cryptocurrencies.
And after 7 days that you join, you will start gaining Bitcoin profits from the AirBit pool.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational introduction does not remain the video’s main purpose: it transitions to “Here’s why more people join Airbit Club,” then explains joining, pooled membership Bitcoin, profit distributions, commissions, and a retirement plan. The buy-and-sell example is hypothetical; it does not demonstrate that AirBit carried out those trades. The closing invitation to start the business confirms that the explanation is also a solicitation.

citations.quote: Here's why more people join Airbit Club.
After you join the club with any of the memberships available, we will use those bitcoins to place them in a pool to start trading cryptocurrencies.
And start your business today.

opening.argument: The offer is described as a membership service with cryptocurrency trading, automated wallet functions, and an affiliate program. Its stated commissions are tied to identifiable events: a referral joining, a membership upgrade, or a matched pair in the organization. That can be read as ordinary service and referral compensation, rather than proof of an illicit mechanism. The excerpts establish that the speaker describes pooling and profit sharing, but do not show a transaction, a viewer’s payment, a credential request, or an independently verified outcome. Those gaps counsel against treating promotional claims as conclusive evidence of fraud.

citations.quote: With an affiliate program that shares Bitcoin to all affiliates
Every time you refer someone to join the club, you will earn 20% of that sale.
every time someone joins your organization on your left leg and another on your right leg you will get 10% Commission's for that match.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to more than referral compensation: the stated core service places membership Bitcoin into a pool and promises profit distributions. Still, its cited excerpts show claims made in a presentation, not evidence that funds were misappropriated or that the described trading did not occur. The matrix and commissions are concerning context, but they do not by themselves establish the truth or falsity of the pool’s operation.

citations.quote: we will use those bitcoins to place them in a pool to start trading cryptocurrencies.
And after 7 days that you join, you will start gaining Bitcoin profits from the AirBit pool.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The question is not whether the video shows a completed transfer or asks for account credentials; it openly urges viewers to join a membership whose Bitcoin is pooled and says members will begin receiving profits after seven days. It also ties compensation to referrals and multi-level organization growth. Describing these as service features does not remove the central investment-pool return promise or its recruitment-linked incentives.
